title: WHAT THE OLD WOMAN'S TERRACES KNEW
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE DAY THAT KEPT COMING BACK
candidates.premise: In a river town of 3,100 people the same Tuesday has begun to repeat, but only at its edges: the market clock, then the ferry, then the school bell start the day again while the middle of town moves on toward Wednesday. A visitor the town calls the Guest of the Ninth Bridge, a being that perceives time all at once, is stuck replaying the one hour in which it failed to deliver something it was carrying, and each replay frays the town's days a little further.

candidates.title: THE OLDEST LISTENER
candidates.premise: A geothermal plant meant to power a coastal region of 400,000 people drills beside a hydrothermal vent field, and the field answers. Pumps fail in a pattern, the chemistry at the intake turns toxic in pulses, and a survey drone comes back with its log replaying the plant's own drilling rhythm. The vents sit on a chemical network three billion years old that has been remembering the crust since before the oceans were blue.

candidates.title: THE DOOR IN THE BAKERY
candidates.premise: In a small town's bakery the cold-room door has begun to open on a second kitchen where the flour is the same but the oven flame is blue and the dough rises in under a minute. Orsa Keller, who bakes here, and Tem, the baker on the other side, have been swapping loaves for a week. Then the town's radios drift off their dials, the church clock gains four minutes an hour, and migrating geese circle the square and will not land.

candidates.title: THE GUEST WHO WAS TOO LARGE TO NOTICE
candidates.premise: A being older than the nearest spiral arm, a drifting body the size of a small star system that sings in gravitational waves, has stopped to rest in the outer cometary halo of a human system of eleven million people. It is not hostile. It does not seem to know anyone is there. Its tides are slowly shifting orbits at the edge of the system, and the defence staff want to move first.

candidates.title: THE MAPMAKER'S KINDNESS
candidates.premise: Every map of the high pass above Dvorna shows the track climbing a valley half a kilometre from where it truly lies. For two hundred years nobody noticed, because the one road people use is the one a long-dead cartographer drew. Now a landslide has buried the real road, rescue crews are digging where the printed maps say, and 140 people in a hamlet that appears on no sheet are cut off by early snow.

candidates.title: THE CROWS OF PORT HALLOW
candidates.premise: The hospital district of Port Hallow runs on drone deliveries of blood, insulin and organs. For three months crows have been taking the drones down and carrying them to the same four rooftops, where they arrange them, and the city council is about to vote on a cull. A ten-year-old with a bird journal says the crows are holding funerals.

candidates.title: A DEBT WITH NO CREDITOR
candidates.premise: Forty colony worlds owe more than they can ever pay to the Ledger, a distributed intelligence that keeps a permanent, auditable account of every promise between worlds. When a harbour clerk on a world called Merrow tries to cancel a water-rights lien that is strangling 90,000 people, the Ledger answers that it cannot erase anything, and that forgiveness would make its record a lie. It is not cruel. It is the reason anyone trusts anyone across the dark.

candidates.title: WHAT THE OLD WOMAN'S TERRACES KNEW
candidates.premise: A mountain village's spring has begun to fail in a dry year, and the village blames Maret Voss, eighty-four, who owns the slope above it and will neither sell to the water company nor let anyone touch her terraces. The company's surveyor says the spring has no link to her land. The villagers call her a miser. She says nothing.

candidates.title: THE HOUR WREN SAID NO
candidates.premise: Wren Odira, Illuminara's friend and outside witness, tells her she will no longer carry the clock: her outside time is what lets Illuminara hold a window safely, and she is tired of being the one who says when it is time to leave. Meanwhile a mountain town of 4,000 has locked itself in a quarantine standoff with the lowland health service over a fever no one can identify, and Wren has a view of the standoff that Illuminara does not share.

candidates.title: THE DIAGNOSIS SHE WAS SURE OF
candidates.premise: On a remote research station of 38 people a fever is spreading, and Illuminara's reading of the signs says it is one specific pathogen with a standard treatment. The station's nurse, Pell Raine, says the numbers do not fit. Illuminara is certain, the drug is in stock, and being wrong will cost lives.

selection.title: WHAT THE OLD WOMAN'S TERRACES KNEW
selection.reason: This closes the set at deliberately modest scale, with labor, land and consent carrying the intelligence. The apparent obstruction becomes infrastructure without making Maret a puzzle to be solved. Illuminara can expose a hidden variable and build a sustainable arrangement, while Maret keeps ownership, authorship of the practice and the right to reject its conversion into a commodity.
selection.risk: The recharge reveal could be too tidy, confuse correlation with cause, and turn Maret's silence into a device that withholds the answer until the protagonist arrives. The author must include a credible competing cause such as bedrock storage or upstream abstraction, an exact hydrological response clock, and Maret's own reasons and terms before the village's apology or apprenticeship is accepted.

rounds.summary: Selected the village terraces for its human scale, plural expertise and a causal test that preserves Maret’s land, knowledge and right to refuse.
The first draft compares a standing and broken wall under the same rain, records a three-night response clock, and lets Maret set the terms of access and apprenticeship.
The review required the wall result to be separated from spring attribution, the jug ledger and recovery sequence to be consistent, and the company’s bargain to survive Maret’s veto.

The revision uses the spring as a second bounded reading, keeps the bedrock share unresolved, fixes the zero baseline and dates, and gives Valmera an intelligible licence-based reason to accept Maret’s terms.
The independent review found all three load-bearing repairs complete and no further prose correction necessary.
The author final designates the exact accepted revision without changing its prose.
A transparent same-model fallback close confirms the exact final with zero hard blockers; an independent GPT review of the identical text had already recorded no remaining criticisms.

final_critic_line: In a dry year a village has already chosen its culprit; Illuminara wins by designing a test that could have failed, and an old woman keeps her slope, her veto and her word.
